title: Baicalin ameliorates interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome by inhibiting the TLR4/NF-kappaB pathway.
authors: Yang, Debin; He, Yuwei; Alimu, Parehe; Cao, Di; Liu, Jianhe
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄酮类化合物BA通过TLR4/NF-kB通路缓解间质性膀胱炎，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS) is a chronic inflammatory bladder disorder characterized by pelvic pain and urinary symptoms, yet effective therapeutic options remain limited. Baicalin (BA), a bioactive flavonoid derived from Scutellaria baicalensis, exhibits anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, though its role in IC/BPS has not been fully elucidated. This study demonstrates that BA significantly ameliorates cyclophosphamide-induced urination frequency and bladder tissue damage and reduces serum levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including TNF-alpha, IL-6, and IL-1beta, in a rat model of IC/BPS. Integrated analysis of network pharmacology, metabolomics, molecular docking, and experimental validation elucidated the potential mechanism by which BA treats IC/BPS through regulation of the TLR4/NF-kappaB signaling pathway.Network pharmacological analysis identified 13 core targets, and both KEGG pathway enrichment and metabolomics results indicated significant enrichment of the NF-kappaB signaling pathway. Molecular docking confirmed strong binding affinities between BA and TLR4, MYD88, and NF-kappaB p65, with binding energies below - 7.0 kcal/mol. Western blot analysis further verified that BA treatment downregulated the expression of these key signaling molecules. These results indicate that BA alleviates IC/BPS primarily by suppressing the TLR4/NF-kappaB pathway, thereby attenuating inflammation and restoring metabolic balance. Our findings provide a mechanistic basis for the application of BA in IC/BPS treatment and support its potential for clinical translation.
abstract_zh: 间质性膀胱炎/膀胱疼痛综合征（IC/BPS）是一种慢性炎症性膀胱疾病，以盆腔疼痛和泌尿系统症状为特征，然而有效的治疗选择仍然有限。黄芩苷（BA），一种源自黄芩的生物活性黄酮类化合物，具有抗炎和抗氧化特性，但其在IC/BPS中的作用尚未完全阐明。本研究证明，在IC/BPS大鼠模型中，BA显著改善环磷酰胺诱导的排尿频率和膀胱组织损伤，并降低血清中促炎细胞因子（包括TNF-α、IL-6和IL-1β）的水平。通过网络药理学、代谢组学、分子对接和实验验证的综合分析，阐明了BA通过调节TLR4/NF-κB信号通路治疗IC/BPS的潜在机制。网络药理学分析确定了13个核心靶点，KEGG通路富集和代谢组学结果均表明NF-κB信号通路显著富集。分子对接证实BA与TLR4、MYD88和NF-κB p65之间具有强结合亲和力，结合能低于-7.0 kcal/mol。Western blot分析进一步验证了BA治疗下调了这些关键信号分子的表达。这些结果表明，BA主要通过抑制TLR4/NF-κB通路来缓解IC/BPS，从而减轻炎症并恢复代谢平衡。我们的发现为BA在IC/BPS治疗中的应用提供了机制基础，并支持其临床转化的潜力。
